about: The vocabulary's own tests: what its queries, shapes, fixtures, features and kits are held to, beside the rules a runtime runs. Each heading names the files it is about.
capabilities: Named questions an app asks a pod · queries/questions/
What each query gives over a small pod · tests/fixtures/*/manifest.ttl
What is true of any pod once its derivations have run · queries/derivations/, ontologies/cascade.ttl
Shapes that find a wrong pod · ontologies/*.shapes.ttl, tests/shape-cases/
Terms declared for everything a pod writes · ontologies/*.ttl
Shapes that check a name against the address it comes from · cascade:ServerRecordNameShape, cascade:ServerNameShape
Shapes that list the codes of an HL7 code system · cascade:DataAbsentReasonCodeShape, cascade:NullFlavorCodeShape, cascade:ObservationInterpretationCodeShape
The order a runtime runs the derivations and a lens in · queries/derivations/, queries/lenses/, ro-crate-metadata.json
Derived state two engines build alike · queries/derivations/, queries/lenses/, queries/views/
Matcher comparisons a runtime binds to records · queries/matcher/, runtime/rule-list/
Rule lists the features and kits carry · runtime/rule-list/, **/references/*.ttl
Feature files any runtime can run · runtime/*.feature, conformance/*/*.feature, runtime/steps.md
C-CDA sections a kit's saved output accounts for · conformance/*/scripted-input/*/downloads/, runtime/scripted-input/*/downloads/
Kinds of record in the queries · queries/derivations/records.rq, queries/views/
The form every query is written in · queries/**/*.rq

glossary.definition: one thing done to a pod that writes files to it: an import, an entry session, a connection to a hospital's server, or a run of the matcher.
the program that converts an export into records; `import` loads it on first use.
Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture: HL7's standard for the XML summary documents patient portals hand out.
a published list of codes for one kind of thing, such as RxNorm for medicines, LOINC for lab tests and SNOMED CT for clinical findings.
one code from one code system, as a record states it.
a query the matcher runs to find records that are one thing; a rule list names each by its path under `queries/matcher/`.
a query whose answer a runtime adds to a pod's derived state, such as the one that says which version of a record is current.
what the derivations and one lens add to a pod's files: statements worked out from them, which the views and questions read.
a file of a person's records as a hospital's server or portal gave it, before any import: FHIR resources in JSON, or a C-CDA document.
a program that runs SPARQL; the tests run every query on two, Oxigraph and rdflib.
one scenario of a feature: a few lines beginning Given, When or Then, which a runtime runs.
a file of rules and examples in Gherkin, the plain-text format Cucumber reads; the rules of a pod are written as features.
a small hand-made pod under `tests/fixtures/`, with a manifest of the rows that queries give over it; each shows one behaviour.
in SHACL, a thing a shape is checked against.
in SPARQL, the patterns between one pair of braces.
Health Level Seven, the body that publishes FHIR, C-CDA and the code systems they use.
a web-style identifier, such as `https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/cascade#Record`; every term and every record is named by one.
a conclusion about records, made by a person or by a machine.

of record: what a record is, such as an allergy or a lab result; `queries/derivations/records.rq` lists them. Of question: `entry`, `record`, `judgment` or `profile`, the one thing a question outside `pod` is about.
a story and the exports it uses, which the vocabulary carries for testing, such as `alex-rivera`.
a choice of which judgments count when a question is answered: `everyday` is the default, and `export` is stricter, for records sent elsewhere.
a Turtle file listing tests in the W3C's test vocabulary: for a fixture, each query and the rows it must give; for the shape cases, each file and what validating it reports.
the part of a runtime that compares a pod's records and writes a Same for those its rules find to be one thing, such as one allergy reported by two sources.
a query the vocabulary carries under a name, such as `pod/My active allergies`.
the common beginning of a vocabulary's IRIs, such as `https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/cascade#`.
a query the vocabulary publishes that gives the name of a thing from what it is made from, such as a record's name from its address on a server.
a Turtle file under `ontologies/` that declares terms.
the wording of a Given, a When or a Then, with its parameters in braces; `runtime/steps.md` lists every one a feature may use.
a stand-in name a query gives a view entry, `urn:cascade:entry:` and a hash, until a runtime writes the entry's real name.
a difficulty put into a kit's data on purpose, numbered such as P7, with a rule and an example that show how a pod handles it.
one person's records, and what that person has said about them, kept as files in one folder.
a derivation's place in the order a runtime runs them, a number the root crate gives it.
a short name a file declares for a namespace, such as `cascade:`.
the comment a query file opens with, saying what its rows are; the site shows it beside the query.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
`ro-crate-metadata.json`, the file at the vocabulary's root that lists its files in the RO-Crate format.
a numbered requirement in the vocabulary that every runtime must meet, such as A14 in `runtime/arrivals.feature`; a heading on this page links the rules its API reaches.
the vocabulary's list of what the matcher compares, each line naming a query and the table kind it reads; it has versions, as a reference table has.
software that reads and writes pods as the vocabulary requires.
the records an adapter made of a kit's download, kept in the kit beside the download.
a part of a C-CDA document with a title, such as Allergies: text for a person to read, and coded statements.
a worked example of a naming rule for a server or a record pulled from one: its inputs and the name they give.
a small Turtle file under `tests/shape-cases/`, valid or broken in one way, with what validating it reports.
the vocabulary's requirements on what a record, a judgment or a file of a pod must state, written in SHACL, the W3C language for checking data.
the W3C query language for data written as statements, as Turtle writes them.
a SELECT written inside another query's group.
a term declared to hold both ways: if A is the same as B, B is the same as A.
what a reference table's rows say, such as product ingredients or vaccine groups; the vocabulary declares each kind.
one word the vocabulary defines, named by an IRI, a web-style identifier such as `https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/cascade#allergen`.
a W3C text format for writing statements in the vocabulary's terms.

a pod's records of one kind, such as medications, as its judgments leave them: one line for each thing however many sources reported it. A named question such as `pod/My medication history` returns a view's rows.
one thing in a view, such as one medication or one lab result: the records that are one thing, shown as one. A row names it in `entry`, by an IRI that ends in `#` and 64 hexadecimal digits.
cascade-vocabulary, the project that defines the words health data is written in, the requirements every pod meets, and a set of ready-made questions.
